T1.implementation_approach: Develop a frontend form to input note details and handle submission using JavaScript.
T1.notes: Ensure form validation for required fields.

T2.implementation_approach: Create an API endpoint to save notes and use a database query to store the data.
T2.notes: Use secure methods to prevent SQL injection.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a schema with fields like note_id, title, content, timestamp, and tags.
T3.notes: Consider indexing for faster search and retrieval.

T4.implementation_approach: Implement a UI feature to categorize or group notes based on tags or folders.
T4.notes: Allow drag-and-drop functionality for better user experience.

T5.implementation_approach: Develop backend logic to organize notes by tags, folders, or custom categories.

T6.implementation_approach: Add a search bar in the UI and implement filtering based on keywords or tags.
T6.notes: Provide real-time search suggestions for better usability.

T7.implementation_approach: Create an API endpoint to query the database for matching notes based on search criteria.
T7.notes: Optimize queries for performance and accuracy.

T8.implementation_approach: Write unit tests to verify note creation functionality and validate form inputs.
T8.notes: Test edge cases like empty fields or invalid data.

T9.implementation_approach: Test the organization feature by simulating user actions like grouping and rearranging notes.

T10.implementation_approach: Test the search functionality by querying notes with various keywords and tags.
T10.notes: Validate results for accuracy and speed.

T11.implementation_approach: Deploy the application using a cloud service and set up CI/CD pipelines for updates.
T11.notes: Ensure proper environment configuration and security measures.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
# app/database.py
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

# Define the database URL (SQLite for simplicity)
DATABASE_URL = "sqlite:///notes_app.db"

# Create the database engine
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})

# Create a configured "Session" class
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)

# Define the declarative base class
Base = declarative_base()

# Export the interfaces
__all__ = ["engine", "SessionLocal", "Base"]
# SQLAlchemy db instance for models
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

from app import db

class Note(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'notes'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    content = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Note {self.title}>'

from flask import Blueprint, request, jsonify
from app.models import Note
from app import db

notes_bp = Blueprint('notes', __name__)

# Route to create a new note
@notes_bp.route('/notes', methods=['POST'])
def create_note():
    data = request.get_json()
    title = data.get('title', '')
    content = data.get('content', '')
    if not title or not content:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Title and content are required'}), 400
    new_note = Note(title=title, content=content)
    db.session.add(new_note)
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify({'message': 'Note created successfully', 'note': new_note.to_dict()}), 201

# Route to get all notes
@notes_bp.route('/notes', methods=['GET'])
def get_notes():
    notes = Note.query.all()
    return jsonify([note.to_dict() for note in notes]), 200

# Route to get a specific note by ID
@notes_bp.route('/notes/<int:note_id>', methods=['GET'])
def get_note(note_id):
    note = Note.query.get(note_id)
    if not note:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Note not found'}), 404
    return jsonify(note.to_dict()), 200

# Route to update a note by ID
@notes_bp.route('/notes/<int:note_id>', methods=['PUT'])
def update_note(note_id):
    data = request.get_json()
    note = Note.query.get(note_id)
    if not note:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Note not found'}), 404
    title = data.get('title', note.title)
    content = data.get('content', note.content)
    note.title = title
    note.content = content
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify({'message': 'Note updated successfully', 'note': note.to_dict()}), 200

# Route to delete a note by ID
@notes_bp.route('/notes/<int:note_id>', methods=['DELETE'])
def delete_note(note_id):
    note = Note.query.get(note_id)
    if not note:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Note not found'}), 404
    db.session.delete(note)
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify({'message': 'Note deleted successfully'}), 200

from flask import Flask, render_template
from app.notes import notes_blueprint
from app.database import db

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.secret_key = "your_secret_key_here"

    # Register blueprints
    app.register_blueprint(notes_blueprint)

    # Initialize database
    with app.app_context():
        db.create_all()

    # Home route
    @app.route('/')
    def home():
        return render_template('index.html')

    return app

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = create_app()
    app.run(debug=True)

    """Create and configure the Flask application."""

    db.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints
    register_blueprints(app)

    # Define home route
    @app.route('/')
    def index():
        return render_template('index.html')

    return app

# Note-Taking Application

An application for creating, organizing, and managing notes.

## Features

- Create Notes: Allows users to create and save text-based notes.
- Organize Notes: Provides functionality to categorize or tag notes for better organization.
- Search Notes: Enables users to search for specific notes using keywords.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
